methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia’s technical workforce faces uncertainty as funding runs out for middle school program
signals.signal_reading: The collapse of GO TEC funding in Virginia's most underserved regions signals failure to build foundational technical capacity where it's needed most, widening the gap as metro areas advance toward AI while rural areas lose even pre-AI technical workforce programs.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: A dedicated WorkAI Lab at Roanoke College represents institutional investment in deep AI capability, but its concentration in a single higher-ed institution signals localized expertise development rather than distributed fluency across the region's broader workforce.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community-based AI workshops led by a Norfolk native represent grassroots peer learning networks that could build distributed, deep capability outside traditional institutional channels—a key marker of the Build It Yourself pathway emerging in a non-NoVA region.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M AI data center infrastructure investment in Henrico concentrates advanced technical capability and 200 specialized jobs in the Richmond metro hub, reinforcing the capital-intensive, geographically concentrated pattern of AI development.

signals.title: Henry County supervisors will consider data centers, battery energy storage in zoning rules
signals.signal_reading: Henry County's consideration of data center zoning represents infrastructure-layer participation in AI economy rather than capability development—Southside positions as power/land provider for AI built elsewhere, signaling shallow engagement with the technology itself.
